claim: A machine-learning deployment strategy's attacker is the attacker model its training environment simulates.
quote: It is used as a platform for the MTD AI model to interact with the adversary.
issue: The agent is built and trained in MTDSimTime against its adversary.

claim: MTTC is an attacker-side effectiveness metric (example from Ho).
quote: It represents the mean time taken for the adversary to successfully compromise the hosts. It average of the durations of attack events of SCAN PORT, EXPLOIT VULN, and BRUTE FORCE for all relevant hosts.
issue: Ho's MTTC is an input feature and reward term with a non-standard definition (mean duration of individual attack events), not one of his evaluation metrics (ASR, ROA, APE, Risk, Sec. 3.4.2). As an example of MTTC in MTD evaluation it is weak.

claim: Risk is a defender-side effectiveness metric (example from Ho).
quote: The change of risk per interval(before and after moving target defense deployment) is measured as an indicator of the effectiveness of the MTD deployment.
issue: Risk is also one of Ho's four evaluation metrics (Sec. 3.4.2). Placing it defender-side follows Cho's classification, the dissertation's mapping.

claim: Time since last MTD is a defender-side effectiveness metric (example from Ho).
quote: Time metrics such as MTD freuqncy and time since last MTD can reflect the immediate changes in the network, including potential attacks.
issue: Ho uses it only as an input feature (all-features model), not to measure how MTD performs; his evaluation metrics are ASR, ROA, APE and Risk. Neither cited source (ho2024, tay2024) uses it as an evaluation metric.
fix_text: drop "; time since last MTD [ho2024, tay2024]" from the effectiveness row
